findings.opportunity: Delta merging loads every domain into the proposed contents map and then invokes the production write function for every domain, including domains whose exact content was not changed by the delta.
findings.impact: Avoid redundant atomic writes, filesystem metadata churn, and rollback entries for unchanged formal domain files. Production writes and production rollback work become proportional to files whose proposed content actually differs, while complete-tree staging and validation remain unchanged.
evidence: src/utils/architecture-delta-merger.ts:67-72 loads every .c4 domain file into contents for discovery.
Only new-domain handling at lines 74-82, matching extend targets at lines 84-89, and relation additions at lines 91-101 can change proposed contents.
src/utils/architecture-delta-merger.ts:116-124 rereads originals and invokes the write abstraction for every contents entry without comparing proposed and original strings.
The formal project currently contains 10 domain files, so a one-domain extension causes production writes for all 10 domains.

src/utils/architecture-delta-merger.ts:103-114 already validates the complete copied architecture tree before any production write, so excluding exact-content-equal files from the later write set does not weaken validation.
Focused current-code validation passed 24 tests across architecture-delta-merger, sync-workflow, and arch-command suites; the worktree was clean and had no staged files.
findings.recommendation: Preserve the full proposed contents map for domain discovery and staged validation, but capture existing domain contents as originals when initially read, capture the original relations content when relevant, derive an ordered changed-files map by exact string comparison, and use only that map for production writes and rollback.
findings.keyDesign: Separate complete proposed-tree state from the production mutation set. Keep contents as the full domain proposal used to populate the staging copy. Keep originals for existing candidates, using null only for newly created files. After all transformations and successful staged validation, filter contents in insertion order to entries whose original is absent or differs exactly. Write only those entries and rollback only those attempted transaction files.
preservationConstraints: The complete staged architecture tree must still be validated before any production write.
All existing domain files must remain available for domain discovery and extend-target resolution.
New domain files must always be treated as changed and removed during rollback if a later production write fails.
Changed existing domain and relations files must retain the current write abstraction and atomicWrite behavior.
Rollback must restore every changed existing file and remove every changed newly created file.
A production write failure must still reject the merge and leave the formal architecture byte-for-byte equivalent to its pre-merge state.
No relation ordering, domain insertion, path formalization, validation timing, error timing before writes, or sync summary behavior may change.
Exact string equality must determine whether a proposed file is unchanged; semantic or formatting normalization must not suppress generated formatting changes.
The verified query adjacency-index optimization in src/commands/arch/query.ts must remain untouched.
implementationOutline: When reading existing domains, populate both the complete proposed contents map and an originals map from the same read results.
For a newly declared domain, record a null original when adding its proposed file.
When relation additions exist, retain current relation parsing and sorting, add the proposed relations content, and record the existing relations content or null if the file was absent.
Keep copying the complete formal architecture and overlaying the complete proposed contents map in staging before LikeC4 validation.
After validation succeeds, derive changed entries in existing Map insertion order using original === null or original !== proposedContent.
Invoke the existing write abstraction only for changed entries.
On write failure, restore or remove only transaction entries, while preserving the existing all-or-nothing formal state guarantee.
Add a unit test with at least two formal domain files and a delta extending only one, asserting the injected writer receives only the changed domain.
Retain and adapt failure-injection coverage so rollback is exercised across two genuinely changed files.
validation: Add or update test/unit/utils/architecture-delta-merger.test.ts to prove an untouched domain is not passed to the injected writer.
